date.label: Undated thematic Leviticus legislation
date.note: This is a literary and thematic grouping in the Sinai narrative, not an independent datable event. No absolute year is inferred.

claims.claim: Leviticus 23 begins with weekly Sabbath and proceeds through annual appointed occasions.
The calendar includes Passover, Unleavened Bread, early harvest offerings, Weeks, seventh-month memorial, the Day of Atonement, and Booths.
Festival law integrates agricultural produce, sacred assemblies, rest, and offerings in varying combinations.
Leviticus 24 regulates the sanctuary lamps and regular bread before narrating a blasphemer case and related laws.
Leviticus 23 should be compared to the related but not identical festivals in Exodus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
claims.evidence: Ex 23:14–19; 34:18–24; Num 28–29; Deut 16; Lev 23, comparing prescribed calendars as texts; Ueoka 2018 full pp. 35–56 on differences and literary organization. Cross-book textual connection, not proof of composition sequence.

claims.claim: Scholars propose different accounts of how Priestly and Holiness festival materials relate within Leviticus 23; no single reconstruction is adopted as a demonstrated composition history.
claims.evidence: Ueoka 2018 full scholarly article pp. 35–56, read directly, proposes Holiness editorial coordination; Rhyder 2019 full article examines Holiness Sabbath/sanctuary practice. Redactional reconstruction remains debated.

claims.claim: Parallels between Leviticus 23 and other biblical festival calendars invite comparison but do not, by themselves, demonstrate direct borrowing or establish a literary date.
claims.evidence: Ex 23, Ex 34, Lev 23, Num 28–29 and Deut 16 are directly comparable biblical legal texts; Ueoka 2018 full pp. 35–56 examines a disputed editorial proposal. No specific ancient Near Eastern borrowing claim is asserted.

connections.note: The founding Passover narrative and Unleavened Bread regulations are earlier in the Pentateuch.
An earlier pilgrimage-festival calendar names agricultural occasions.
A second festival legislation provides a comparison.
Festival descriptions overlap and differ in emphasis.
A postexilic narrative describes renewed observance of Booths.
The Gospel locates major scenes within the Feast of Booths.
Pentecost reflects the later Jewish festival of Weeks.
Talionic formulations provide legal parallels to Leviticus 24:17–22.
